claims.statement: `propose()` in `src/hypermnesic/propose.py` is the single front door for organizing writes: the sidecar extractor, navigation surface, salience digest, connection suggestions, capture triage and daily review all hand path-scoped `Change` records to it instead of holding any write privilege of their own.

`propose()` makes the caller declare the target scope: `allowlist` is a required keyword argument, and every change's path is passed through `serialize.check(repo, path, allowlist=...)` before any other work happens.

In `propose()`, the path guard runs on every path first and each file's new text is then computed in memory by the frontmatter gate for all files, both before any branch exists, so a refused path or an unrequested-frontmatter-drift abort leaves no proposal branch, no PR call and no audit entry, and a multi-file proposal aborts as a whole rather than partially.

The proposal commit is created by `serialize.branch_commit_transaction()` inside a temporary git worktree on a new `hypermnesic/proposals/<slug>` branch cut from base, so the owner's live `HEAD` and working tree are untouched and any failure rolls the half-built branch back; the content reaches the base branch only through the owner's merge.

Approval is an owner-only merge outside the engine: `propose()` only creates the branch commit and optionally opens a PR through the `gh_create` hook with a what/why/source body — no merge verb exists in that code path.

With no PR hook available the proposal branch and its diff still exist locally with `pr_skipped` true, and the `.hypermnesic/proposals.json` ledger lets a later run resume PR creation on the same branch instead of creating a second one.

Re-proposing against an existing slug branch is a reconciliation rather than a re-commit: identical content resolves to `noop`, an existing branch is never given new content, and that limitation is why the navigation surface and daily review derive content-hash slugs (`nav-surface-<sha8>`, `daily-review-<sha8>`) while the salience digest and connection suggestions reuse fixed slugs.

Proposal routing is two-tier: a proposal whose every change is a new file at `HEAD` inside an immutable append zone (`IMMUTABLE_APPEND_ZONES`, i.e. `sources/`) takes the fast path and commits per file straight to `HEAD` with `fast_path=True` and `branch=None`, while an existing file or any curated path always becomes a gated proposal branch.

`ProposalBudget` caps proposal-branch creation per UTC calendar day and is charged only when a real branch is created, so no-ops and fast-path commits cost nothing; the cap is an optional `propose()` parameter that the shipped emitters do not pass yet.

`safe_slug()` neutralises caller-supplied titles that otherwise reach `git` and `gh` as arguments: it strips `..`, restricts the charset to alphanumerics plus `-_/`, forbids a leading `-` or `/`, bounds the length to 60 characters and falls back to `proposal`.

The proposal gate is computed against committed `HEAD` content, not the working tree: a file absent at `HEAD` is rendered fresh from `set_fields` plus body with no drift check, an existing file goes through `frontmatter_gate.gated_edit`, and a proposal whose gated result equals `HEAD` is reported as `noop` with no branch.
A created proposal appends one audit entry with `verb="propose"`, the comma-joined target paths, base `HEAD` as `old_sha` and the branch commit as `new_sha`, carrying the summary but never page body.

`generated.render()` forces two demarcations on every generated artifact — `generated_by: hypermnesic` in frontmatter, merged underneath the caller's keys so it cannot be omitted, and a visible managed block bounded by the `[!hypermnesic]` callout and `<!-- /hypermnesic:generated -->` — and `is_generated()` detects the frontmatter marker, which is how memory control derives the `generated` source type.

Regeneration is whole-file, not surgical: the dashboard builders render a complete replacement through `generated.render()` and propose it as the note's new content, so a merged replacement discards hand edits both inside and outside the managed region; the marker states the overwrite contract but no code preserves text from the previous file.

The Obsidian Bases view configuration cannot carry a callout, so `nav_surface.build_base_config()` writes `generated_by: hypermnesic` into the YAML plus a leading comment stating edits are overwritten, and the config uses exactly one filter root group (`all`) and one table view.

Salience scores every indexed path deterministically as `0.4 · (link_degree / max_link_degree) + 0.3 · centrality + 0.3 · write_recency`, where centrality is the mean cosine of a note's stored vectors to every other note (0.0 with fewer than two paths) and write recency is rank-normalised across distinct audit timestamps; notes sort by score then path and are flagged `dormant` below `dormancy_threshold` (default 0.5).

There is no read or access signal in salience: recency means recency of write, a path with no audit entry scores zero and is dormant by construction, and no `salience:` field is ever written into a source note's frontmatter — the ranking lives only in the generated digest.

`salience.score_notes()` forces unbudgeted full embedding coverage before computing centrality and reports `coverage_complete=False` when the embedder is absent or fails mid-fill, so a partial centrality is labelled while scores are still produced.

The spaced-review digest lists salient-but-dormant notes ranked by structural importance only — raw link degree plus centrality, deliberately excluding recency — capped at `top_n` (default 10), and proposes them as the generated `dashboards/salience-digest.md` note under the `dashboards/` scope, saying so explicitly when nothing is dormant.

A connection candidate must be both similar and unlinked: cosine at or above the threshold (default 0.83), strictly below the near-duplicate cutoff (default 0.999), and joined to the other note by no existing body-wikilink edge in either direction; candidates are sorted deterministically by similarity then path and capped per run, and `connection_proposals()` returns `None` rather than an empty note when nothing qualifies.

Connection suggestions never write a wikilink into a source note — they are proposed as the generated `dashboards/connection-suggestions.md` note — and when vectors are derived from the index a full unbudgeted embed runs first so an unembedded note cannot hide a genuine pair.

The navigation surface emits `dashboards/MOC.md` and `dashboards/overview.base` as one proposal under the `dashboards/` scope (never the guard-protected `views/`), with a content-hash slug over the rendered pair; the MOC lists every indexed path, up to five distinct recently-changed paths from the audit log, and optional links to the salience, connection and daily-review surfaces supplied by the caller.

The daily review composes the capture backlog with its triage stages, up to five recent audit-log writes, the supplied generated-surface links, recall-mode reminders, the five memory-control cleanup commands and the degraded-state note, and proposes it at `dashboards/daily-review.md` without moving, deleting or rewriting any source note.

`hypermnesic daily-review <repo> [--json]` is the command for the daily loop: it reads the audit log and passes `gh_create=None`, so the review always lands as a local proposal branch with `pr_skipped` true, and it defaults the linked surfaces to `dashboards/MOC.md` and `dashboards/salience-digest.md` with no connections link unless `--connections-rel` is given.

A repo with no `index.db` still produces a daily review, with the CLI attaching a `partial: no index found; review uses files/audit only` degraded note, because the note is composed from the on-disk capture backlog, the audit log and the supplied links rather than from the index.

The navigation, digest and connection builders are library entry points today: no CLI subcommand or registered MCP tool invokes `nav_proposal`, `digest_proposal` or `connection_proposals`, and the daily review only links their conventional paths, which is the extension point a future command or proposal-inbox surface would use.
